title: Epoxy RFID Keyfob — IP68 Outdoor-Rated Credential
summary: Epoxy RFID keyfobs pot the inlay in a seamless resin dome over a PVC / PET / aluminium substrate, giving IP68 by construction. The 30-50 mm teardrop, rectangle or custom die-cut body carries a 3-5 mm dome with CMYK artwork under crystal-clear resin. The envelope clears IEC 60068-2-78 damp-heat, IEC 60068-2-52 salt-mist, 1.5 m drop, ATEX Zone 2 passive-equipment use and NEMA 4X wash-down for industrial, outdoor and food-plant access control.

brief.label: Form factor
items: Teardrop / rectangle / oval / custom die-cut 30-50 mm × 20-35 mm with 3-5 mm epoxy dome height; 6-14 g mass; Ø 4-6 mm key-ring hole.
Optional metal keyring grommet insert in the pierced hole to carry the lanyard load instead of the substrate.

brief.label: Air-interface envelope
items: 13.56 MHz HF — ISO 14443 Type A/B (MIFARE Classic 1K, MIFARE Plus SE, MIFARE DESFire EV3, NTAG 213/215/216, NTAG 424 DNA).
125 kHz LF — EM4200 / {chip:em-microelectronic-em4305:short_name} / {chip:atmel-t5577:name} / HID ProxCard II-compatible clones for legacy reader estates.

brief.label: Encapsulation chemistry
items: Two-component epoxy — bisphenol-A-epichlorohydrin (CAS 25068-38-6) with aliphatic-amine or cycloaliphatic-amine hardener; UV-stabilised and HALS-extended for outdoor.
Pot-life 20-40 min; gel-time 1-2 h at 25 °C; full cure 24 h; Shore D hardness 75-85.

brief.label: Ingress + durability
items: IP68 per IEC 60529 by construction (fully encapsulated resin — no seam for ingress).
IEC 60068-2-32 Ea drop 1.5 m; IEC 60068-2-6 vibration 5-500 Hz 2 h / axis; IEC 60068-2-64 random vibration for transport.

brief.label: Climate envelope
items: IEC 60068-2-78 damp-heat steady 40 °C / 93 % RH for 4 days; IEC 60068-2-14 thermal cycling -40 °C to +85 °C × 10 cycles.
IEC 60068-2-52 salt-mist cycling for coastal / outdoor service; 500-hour QUV for UV-stabilised resin variants.

brief.label: Chemical resistance
items: Fully cured epoxy is resistant to typical facility cleaners, IPA wipe-down, dilute acids / bases, hydrocarbons, quat ammonia and NEMA 4X wash-down chemistry.
Continuous immersion in aggressive solvents (MEK, toluene, concentrated acids) is out of envelope — move to PTFE / silicone housing for those cases.

brief.label: Hazardous-area posture
items: ATEX 2014/34/EU passive-equipment compatible in Zone 2 (gas) / Zone 22 (dust) when paired with an ATEX-certified reader; the fob itself is passive with zero stored energy.
IECEx / AS/NZS 60079 parallel conformity; NFPA 70 Class I Div 2 acceptable under the passive-equipment clause.

brief.label: Decoration + branding
items: 4-colour CMYK or Pantone-matched artwork printed on the substrate before epoxy pot; crystal dome magnifies the artwork ≈ 1.1-1.3×.
Laser-engraved serial number on the reverse aluminium / PVC base; custom die-cut brand silhouette on special-order SKUs.

brief.label: Chemistry + disclosure
items: RoHS 3 + REACH SVHC cleared on the cured-resin + hardener + pigment system; California Prop 65 disclosure on consumer-facing SKUs.
Halogen-free substrate and ink options; bio-based epoxy variants (bisphenol-F / bio-glycidyl ether) available for sustainability programmes.

brief.label: Integration
items: Same Wiegand 26 / 34 / 37 + OSDP v2.2 Secure Channel + MIFARE DESFire EV3 + NTAG 424 DNA stack as the ABS variant; PACS sees an identical credential.
Factory TID read-only (ISO 14443 / ISO 18000-63 as applicable); EPC / NDEF permalocked at issuance.

brief.label: Operating envelope summary
items: -40 °C to +85 °C service; IP68 by construction; ATEX Zone 2 / 22 passive clearance; NEMA 4X wash-down.
Typical field life 7-12 years under outdoor / industrial carry (longer than ABS thanks to seamless encapsulation).

heroPoints: Seamless epoxy encapsulation — IP68 by construction, not by seal; fob cleared against IEC 60068-2-78 damp-heat, IEC 60068-2-52 salt-mist cycling, IEC 60068-2-14 thermal cycling -40 °C to +85 °C, 1.5 m drop and 5-500 Hz vibration.
ATEX Zone 2 / 22 passive-equipment compatible when paired with an ATEX reader — zero stored energy on the fob qualifies it under the passive-equipment clause for chemical / fuel / flour-mill sites.

sections.title: Why outdoor and industrial access control outgrows an ultrasonically-welded ABS shell
bullets: Ultrasonic-welded ABS keyfobs carry a weld seam along the fob perimeter; after 5-7 years of outdoor UV + thermal cycling, the weld relaxes and water / chemical ingress becomes the dominant failure mode. Sealed-by-construction epoxy has no such seam.

NEMA 4X food-plant CIP / SIP wash-down chemistry (quat ammonia, peracetic acid, caustic soda, chlorinated alkaline) attacks ABS at concentrations seen routinely on the process floor; cured epoxy tolerates the same chemistry indefinitely.

ATEX Zone 2 / 22 gas / dust sites require passive-equipment clearance for any item clipped to the worker; the epoxy fob qualifies under the passive-equipment clause because it stores zero energy and has no mechanical fault that could produce a spark.

Outdoor-industrial sites pair a 500-hour QUV + 720-hour salt-fog environment with 5-10 years of daily outdoor carry; UV-stabilised / HALS-extended epoxy holds the crystal dome optical clarity and surface hardness across that envelope.
Branded / die-cut silhouettes that matter to hospitality, theme-park, event and promotional programmes are far easier in epoxy than in injection-moulded ABS (no tool-up cost per silhouette).

sections.title: Epoxy vs ABS vs metal — where the envelope boundary sits
bullets: ABS ultrasonically-welded — default office / campus / fleet keyfob; IP68 for 5-10 years under office conditions; not rated for ATEX, NEMA 4X, continuous outdoor UV / salt-fog or custom die-cut silhouettes.

Epoxy-encapsulated — upgrade path to outdoor / industrial / food-plant / ATEX Zone 2 sites; IP68 by construction; NEMA 4X wash-down-proof; ATEX-compatible; UV-stabilised for outdoor; crystal-dome optical for branded artwork.

Metal-housed (stainless / zinc / aluminium) — where mechanical robustness and nickel-release / food-contact chemistry matter most; heavier (15-30 g) and more expensive; different decoration path (laser engraving).

Material choice is a trade-off between mechanical robustness, chemical envelope, ATEX posture, decoration flexibility and unit cost; the three housings cover the full envelope the access-control estate faces.
The inlay, chip, PACS integration and credential workflow are identical across all three housings — only the outer material changes.

before: Weld seam along perimeter; UV + thermal cycling relaxes the weld at 5-7 years of outdoor carry.

Not cleared for ATEX Zone 2 / 22 unless specifically re-certified per site.
Injection-mould tool cost makes per-silhouette branded die-cuts economically unviable under 20k MOQ.
after: Seamless resin pot — no weld seam for ingress; IP68 holds for 7-12 years of outdoor / industrial carry.
Cured epoxy resistant to quat ammonia, peracetic acid, caustic soda, hydrocarbons and IPA wipe-down.
ATEX Zone 2 / 22 passive-equipment clause applies (zero stored energy); paired with ATEX reader.
Custom die-cut silhouette at no tool-up cost per shape; crystal dome magnifies CMYK / Pantone artwork.

sections.title: Where epoxy keyfobs earn their place in the catalogue
bullets: Chemical-plant and refinery access — ATEX Zone 2 gas site; epoxy fob on every contractor / employee lanyard; paired with an ATEX-certified reader at each area entrance.
Food-plant and beverage-plant — NEMA 4X wash-down zones; FSMA 21 CFR 117 HACCP programmes require non-shedding, cleanable credentials that survive daily CIP spray.
Pharma GMP / vaccine-production plants — 21 CFR 211 Current Good Manufacturing Practice; cleanable, non-particulate credentials acceptable in clean-room ancillary areas (grade D / C).
Marine and offshore — salt-fog + UV + vibration; epoxy survives 720-hour salt-fog cycling better than any ABS weld under the same conditions.
Theme park, stadium and event — custom die-cut branded silhouette on every guest / staff credential; CMYK artwork preserved under crystal dome for the multi-day event span.

University / hospitality loyalty — promotional branded fob with {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:short_name} SUN payload for tap-to-reveal content; fob becomes a brand touchpoint rather than a plain credential.

sections.title: How to roll out an epoxy keyfob programme across an outdoor / industrial estate
bullets: Start from the reader estate: confirm ATEX / IECEx / NEMA 4X reader certification at each zone entrance; the epoxy fob qualifies under the passive-equipment clause once paired with a certified reader.
Choose the chip per security posture, same as for ABS — EM4200 / T5577 legacy HID-compatible; MIFARE DESFire EV3 for ISO/IEC 27001 AES-128; NTAG 424 DNA for consumer / guest / BYOD tap.
For food / pharma plants, confirm the cured-epoxy material safety-data sheet clears 21 CFR 117 and 21 CFR 211 non-shedding / non-particulate posture; no un-cured resin on shelf after QA.
UV-stabilised / HALS-extended resin is mandatory for outdoor / offshore; specify ≥ 500-hour QUV + 720-hour salt-fog as acceptance criteria on the incoming lot.
Branded die-cut silhouette — lock the artwork file and Pantone palette before pot; the crystal dome magnifies artwork 1.1-1.3× so artwork tolerance is tighter than flat-printed ABS.

Disposal — cured epoxy is not melt-recyclable; landfill-disposal or specialised thermoset-composite recycling stream per WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU Art. 8(5); chip rendered inoperative per NIST SP 800-88 before disposal.

items.label: Weeks 5-6 — encode + issue workflow

faq.question: Is the epoxy keyfob ATEX Zone 2 / 22 certified?
faq.answer: The fob qualifies under the passive-equipment clause of ATEX 2014/34/EU rather than carrying its own certificate. It is a passive transponder with zero stored energy and no mechanical fault mode capable of producing a spark, so the clause applies — alongside the parallel IECEx / AS/NZS 60079 / NFPA 70 Class I Div 2 rules — when the fob is paired with an ATEX-certified reader. Formal Zone 2 / 22 clearance is carried by the reader, not the fob; this is how virtually every passive-RFID hazardous-area credential is structured.

faq.question: Can the epoxy keyfob survive food-plant CIP / SIP wash-down?
faq.answer: Yes — cured epoxy is chemically resistant to typical food-plant CIP / SIP chemistry (quat ammonia 200-400 ppm, peracetic acid 80-150 ppm, caustic soda 1-2 % at 60-80 °C) for the tens-of-minutes contact times normal in daily wash-down. Sustained high-concentration hot-caustic or aggressive solvent immersion (MEK, toluene) sits outside envelope; for those cases switch to a silicone or PTFE-overmoulded housing.

faq.question: How does the crystal dome impact artwork tolerance?
faq.answer: The cured epoxy dome acts as a plano-convex lens with ≈ 1.1-1.3× optical magnification at the centre of the dome. This magnifies both the artwork and any print defect, so artwork production lane tolerance is tighter than for a flat-printed ABS fob: Pantone match verification on the printed substrate before pot is recommended, and CMYK raster artwork should be delivered at ≥ 300 dpi to avoid visible print pattern under the dome.
